subject: Culture
title: The Kula Ring
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on The Kula Ring.

hook.text: In Papua New Guinea, shell necklaces travel clockwise and armbands travel counterclockwise across islands—endlessly.

buildup.text: Bronisław Malinowski documented the Kula ring in 1922—a gift exchange system spanning thousands of miles of ocean.

discovery.text: The items have no practical use. Their value comes from their history: who held them and for how long.

twist.text: The Kula ring built trust between islands that were otherwise rivals. Gift exchange prevented war.

climax.text: Economists compare the Kula to modern financial instruments—tokens of trust circulating to maintain relationships.

punchline.text: Some gifts are valuable because they won't stop moving.
